::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 18th 1861  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1861/6
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd),

I think your answer is a very wise one, and quite what I can understand. I am sure with all the poor I have known unusual help unless on some very pressing occasion would be anything but really beneficial, but the three old couples might be most happily provided, and I hope [Mrs Elphinstone](people/person_482.qmd) may choose that way of spending the sum. I will put what you say before her, thank you much for so answering. Thanks too for the Mothers’ Meeting particulars. I put one or two points as notes to the longer letter, which I think they help out greatly - though the object is different. I really think it might be a good time to stir [Mr Mozley](people/person_1065.qmd) up about reprinting those stories of yours. [Frances](other_books/otherbook_265.qmd) would come in well upon the sensation caused by [My Life and What Shall I do with it](other_books/otherbook_297.qmd) I send the first proof of the [Websters](other_books/otherbook_275.qmd), who look well in print, but must wait a month. I thought I should have had a great deal of room when [the stepmother](cmy_books/cmybook_38.qmd) and [the pilgrim](other_books/otherbook_180.qmd) were both done, but there always seems to be less than ever. About [the ladies](cmy_books/cmybook_43.qmd), whom I rather propose to call ‘More precious than rubies’ I shall be very glad of [Mrs Grant](people/person_1825.qmd), and perhaps if you will do the other that you were thinking of first, we might then see about [Mrs Carter](people/person_1830.qmd). The fact is that [my mother](people/person_1606.qmd) knows her nearly by heart, and is much inclined to her, but a little in doubt whether she shall have time to undertake her, having something else just now about which she is busy, and if you were otherwise employed, I should rather like this to decide itself. Lady Russell, [Mrs Hutchinson](people/person_1834.qmd) and [Caroline Perthes](people/person_1827.qmd) have been beautifully done by the author of Magdalen Stafford[^1], [Olimpia Moratea](people/person_1849.qmd) by [Miss Taylor](people/person_1397.qmd), and likewise a wonderful [Mum Bet](people/person_1846.qmd), an American slave whom she extracted from [Miss Martineau](people/person_1724.qmd)’s American book. I have a Russian lady too who has delighted me much [Mme Svetchine](people/person_1848.qmd), whom I translated from the French. I fear I shall still be long in finishing my own part.

yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to Miss Ann Smith/ Rectory/ Old Charlton/ SE and postmarked Winchester 18 March 1861 and London SE 19 March 1861.
[^2]: The identity of the person who published the novel *Magdalen Stafford* and other works as 'the author of Magdalen Stafford' is puzzling, but she may perhaps be the [Mrs Bromfield](people/person_162.qmd) whom CMY called 'one of my crack authors'.
